d.d: All; every; qualifying a singular noun, indicating all examples of the thing so named seen as individual or separate items (compare every).
d.x: Make sure you wash each bowl well.

d.d: Individually; separately; used in a sentence with a plural subject to indicate that the action or state described by the verb applies to all members of the described group individually, rather than collectively to the entire group.
d.x: We ordered half a chicken each, but we each got a whole one.

d.d: Every one/thing individually or one by one.
d.x: I'm going to give each of you a chance to win.

d.d: An individual item: the least quantitative unit in a grouping.
